anomalies.observed: The LM1117-5.0 regulator U3 has both its input (pin 3, VIN) and its output (pin 2, VOUT) connected to the same +5V power flag; the +5V rail is also the board's main input (J1 PWR pin 2). The separate VCC rail used by the fan high-side switch and the analog pull-ups (R2, C3, C1, JP2.2, Q3.2) is not connected to the regulator output at all.
anomalies.expected: By the part's own metadata a 5.0 V LDO needs VIN higher than VOUT (input+dropout) and its VOUT must drive the regulated VCC rail. Tying VIN to the same +5V net as VOUT bypasses/shorts the regulator and leaves VCC without a source.

evidence.quote: U3 ... pin3 VIN '+5V' ... pin2 VOUT '+5V' ... 'LM1117-5.0' (sheet /, page 2 top)
VCC net on R2, C3 100nF, C1 100nF, JP2.2, Q3.2 (sheet /, page 1 top-right / mid)

anomalies.impact: The regulator performs no regulation and its input is shorted to its output; the VCC rail that powers the fan P-FET source and the analog pull-up network is left undriven, so the fan high-side switch has no supply and the board's regulated rail is missing.

anomalies.observed: The I2C_PWR jumper J2 bridges +5V (pin 1) to NET0008 (pin 2). NET0008 is the MOSI/ISP line, also wired to J3.4 (MOSI), J6.2 and MCU pin 5 (PB0/MOSI).
anomalies.expected: A power-enable jumper should not connect the +5V supply to a SPI data / ISP programming line; MOSI must remain a data net driven by the MCU.

evidence.quote: J3 AVR-ISP-6 pin4 'MOSI' 'NET0008'; U4 pin5 'NET0008' (sheet /, page 1/2)

anomalies.impact: When J2 is closed, +5V is shorted onto the MOSI/ISP net, conflicting with the MCU's PB0 output and corrupting/shorting the in-circuit programming line.
